title: Denavit-Hartenberg Convention: Frames, Parameters and Forward Kinematics
learning_objectives: Explain how the Denavit-Hartenberg (DH) convention standardises coordinate frames for serial robot manipulators.
Identify joint axes and assign consecutive frames from the relationship between their z axes.
Interpret the four DH parameters (theta, d, a and alpha), including which one varies for revolute and prismatic joints.
Distinguish frame assignment for skew, parallel and intersecting joint axes.
Use the ordered DH transforms and the chain rule to find the end-effector pose.

outline.content: Recap the motivation: arbitrary frames need six parameters per link, while DH frames need only four. Using the link geometry, introduce the four parameters theta_i, d_i, a_i and alpha_i. Focus on purpose here and define each parameter in the following activities.
Students label the diagram with the four DH parameters. theta_i is the rotation about z_(i-1), d_i the offset along z_(i-1), a_i the length along x_i, and alpha_i the twist about x_i.

outline.topic: Four Motions in the Correct Order
outline.content: Write a short passage on the ordered transform from frame {i-1} to frame {i}. Rotate by theta_i about z_(i-1), translate d_i along z_(i-1), translate a_i along x_i, then rotate by alpha_i about x_i. Key terms: joint angle, link offset, link length, link twist, previous z axis, new x axis.

outline.topic: Which Joint Does z0 Belong To?
outline.content: Using the two-joint robot, ask which axes are the actuation axes of joints 1 and 2. Correct answer: z_0 for joint 1 and z_1 for joint 2, since z_(i-1) belongs to joint i. Distractors are off by one or confuse link axes with joint axes. Feedback distinguishes joints, numbered 1 to n, from links, numbered 0 to n.

Recap the frame assignment steps: place every z_i along a joint axis, choose the base frame, then choose each x_i and origin O_i from how z_(i-1) and z_i relate. y_i then follows from the right-hand rule. Explain the three cases: skew axes use the common normal, parallel axes have many possible common normals, and intersecting axes have a common normal of zero length.

Ask which image shows consecutive joint axes z_(i-1) and z_i that intersect. Correct answer: Image C, where x_i is perpendicular to the plane of both axes and a_i is zero. Images A and B show skew and parallel axes.

outline.topic: Assign Parameters for a Parallel-Axis Link
outline.content: The single revolute link has z_0 and z_1 parallel and pointing the same way. Ask which DH row is correct. Correct answer: theta_1 is the joint variable, d_1 = 0, a_1 is the link length and alpha_1 = 0. Distractors swap d and a, set alpha to 90 degrees, or treat theta as a prismatic displacement.

Use the SCARA robot to test that a revolute joint's variable is the angle theta and a prismatic joint's variable is the displacement d. Also test that theta may include a fixed home-position offset and that a_i is the link length.

outline.topic: What Happens When the Axes Intersect?
outline.content: The example has theta_i = 30 degrees, d_i = 20 cm and alpha_i = 90 degrees. Ask which DH parameter must be zero when the axes intersect and O_i lies on the intersection. Correct answer: a_i = 0. Distractors pick theta_i, d_i or alpha_i; feedback explains that the offset and twist can still be non-zero.

outline.topic: From the DH Table to Forward Kinematics
outline.content: Recap that each DH row gives a homogeneous transform from frame {i-1} to frame {i}: Rz(theta_i), Tz(d_i), Tx(a_i), Rx(alpha_i). Using the chain-rule image, show that the end-effector pose is the ordered product of these transforms, and its translation part is the tool position. Mention the lecture's warning about home-position angle offsets.

Use Lecture Example 1: l_1 = 3, l_2 = 4, theta_1 = 25 degrees, theta_2 = 40 degrees, theta_3 = 0 and l_3 = 0. Ask which expression gives the end-effector x coordinate in frame {0}. Correct answer: 3*cos(25 degrees) + 4*cos(65 degrees), approximately 4.409. Distractors use theta_2 alone instead of the accumulated angle, swap sine and cosine, or subtract the link terms.

Review the key ideas: z_(i-1) is the axis of joint i; theta and d act along the previous z axis, a and alpha along the new x axis; parallel versus intersecting axes, with a = 0 for intersecting axes; revolute theta versus prismatic d and home-angle offsets; forward kinematics as an ordered product of transforms.
